comments.author: @simplykody7248
comments.text:
Don't get me wrong, the game plays well.. but man, as a Rs player for over 20 years.. it feels like they don't know what they're doing when it comes to balance, progression and even the identity. I assume if they didn't have all these deadlines then it would've been better.

Rs has every bit of identity this game could ever ask for, but they're choosing to do a lil bit of rs and whatever else they can conjure up. Feels... wrong imo. Why am i riding a mount and not teleporting places? Why isn't there teleport jewelry? Why am i killing 5 variants of rats, cows, Garou (w/e these are)? Why am i getting full obsidian armor with an addy scimmy? How is a Dorg bow somehow a legendary weapon? It's lvl 28 to weild is the Maingame lol. Why is the whip/granite maul in the early game but without any of the identity that we all know and love? Why take these half measures? I'm 100% confident that if they took all of their inspiration from RS instead of making up new stuff, that the game would be loved more by the fans and the newbies who might want to check out RS3 or OSRS would have a better time porting over, actually knowing the items instead of being vaguely taught about what the OG games are like. Why is getting dragon armor easier than rune? Why not add GP as a currency instead of all these made up currencies? There's a lack of cohesion and it makes the finer details that are lacking stick out like a sore thumb. K, rant over

comments.author: @davidgarza4592
comments.text:
Dragonwilds vet here with over 185 hours in my main world, plus around 4-5k hours on OSRS. Unfortunately, they missed pretty hard with this update. The raid is too easy, there are too many bugs, and the progression didn't quite make sense, you could get full dragon well before ever gathering enough resources to make full rune.

That said, I'm still enjoying it a lot, and it's only a few minor tweaks away from being something players could sink hundreds of hours into for progression. I think the game is just getting started, and I'm hopeful it develops the way OSRS did, with endgame content continuously pushing the vets and raising the ceiling on progression and the time needed to reach it.

Two things I'd love to see soon:

Scalable raid difficulty. Raids in OSRS can scale in difficulty. Right now the raid in Dragonwilds (ignoring the bug where monsters don't respawn) is very easy for an experienced player. It could be so much more engaging if I could scale it, imagine the first Black Dragon room having 3 dragons, or the Abyssal demon room having 2 dragons and 2 demons. The number of mobs, their health, and their damage all scaling with the difficulty would be so cool.
Dragon items as recipes. Dragon gear should have been craftable from recipes, with killing Kuldra dropping the dragon-tier materials you need. Something like 55-75 Kuldra kills on average to gather enough for the full set (higher difficulty tiers giving greater rewards and more materials) would make reaching tier 9 far more meaningful.

I've got a lot more suggestions, but I figured I'd lend the perspective of a degen. Had these two changes been in from the start of 1.0, the fun would have lasted so much longer. That's essentially what OSRS is, players love it for the grind, and Dragonwilds' endgame should be a similar grind, or it gets boring fast.

All that said, the game has terrific bones, and I'm hopeful we'll see changes soon that really let us sink our teeth in further. I haven't enjoyed OSRS in a while now, so this has been really refreshing!
